annotations.description: Attacking with Temple Garden (a 1/1 earthbent land-creature) into a board where the opponent has a Sunpearl Kirin (2/1) and an Otter Token (1/1) that could block. While the opponent's creatures are marked as summoning sick in the snapshot, the decision reasoning itself acknowledges they might not be summoning sick. If they can block, Temple Garden dies and returns tapped, costing a mana source for a turn. Even if unblocked, 1 damage is marginal. The risk-reward ratio of potentially losing a mana-producing land for 1 damage is questionable, especially when Opus Analyst has Appa and Interdimensional Web Watch in hand that need mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Temple Garden (1/1 earthbent land) for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack. Keep Temple Garden untapped as a mana source and potential blocker. The 1 damage is not worth the risk of losing tempo on mana development when you have expensive cards like Appa (4 mana) and Interdimensional Web Watch (4 mana) in hand.

annotations.description: Airbend exiles the target creature (with the option to cast it for {2} later). The player targeted their own Temple Garden (which was an earthbent land-creature with a +1/+1 counter), exiling their own land. This loses them a land/mana source and the +1/+1 counter from earthbend. Meanwhile, the opponent has a Sunpearl Kirin (2/1 flyer) and an Otter token that could have been exiled instead to remove threats. The player's reasoning shows confusion about what airbend does, leading them to exile their own valuable permanent rather than an opponent's creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Temple Garden (own earthbent land-creature) with airbend, exiling it.
annotations.betterLine: Target Sunpearl Kirin to exile the opponent's 2/1 flash flyer, removing a threat. Alternatively, target the Otter Token to shrink the opponent's board. Either would have been far better than exiling your own land.

annotations.description: Casting Appa with no nonland permanents on board wastes its powerful airbend ETB ability. Appa has flash, so there's no reason to cast it now in postcombat main when it could be held.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Appa, Steadfast Guardian in postcombat main with no nonland permanents to airbend.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Airbender Ascension ({1}{W}) this turn, then hold Appa (which has flash) for a future turn when the Ascension is on board to airbend it. This would let Appa airbend the Ascension, and recasting it from exile for {2} would trigger both Appa's token creation and Ascension's quest counter.

annotations.description: The player's reasoning references 'Llanowar Elves' which does not appear to be on the battlefield, indicating confusion about the board state. Additionally, using Map tokens before playing a land (Floodfarm Verge enters untapped for free) is incorrect sequencing - you should play the land first to have maximum mana available. At 4 life, every decision is critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to activate a Map token before playing a land, based on reasoning about a nonexistent Llanowar Elves.
annotations.betterLine: Play Floodfarm Verge first (enters untapped, free), then use Map tokens or other abilities with full mana available. Temple Garden should NOT be played as paying 2 life at 4 life is extremely dangerous.

annotations.description: At 4 life, played Starting Town (enters tapped past turn 3, costs 1 life for colored mana) instead of Floodfarm Verge or Hushwood Verge which enter untapped and produce colored mana for free. The reasoning incorrectly states Starting Town 'gains 1 life' - it does not. Starting Town is strictly worse here.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Starting Town from hand, which enters tapped and requires 1 life payment for colored mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Floodfarm Verge or Hushwood Verge, both of which enter untapped and produce colored mana without any life cost - critical at 4 life.

annotations.description: Grk41F Detect passed on casting any spells during combat with an unblocked Otter Token. Casting Nowhere to Run targeting the animated Hushwood Verge (a creature with +1/+1 counter) would trigger prowess on the Otter, dealing 2 instead of 1 to an opponent at 4 life. Additionally, Kaito's Ninjutsu could replace the unblocked Otter to put a 3/4 attacker through, dropping Opus to 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Nowhere to Run targeting Hushwood Verge to kill the animated land and trigger prowess, or use Kaito's Ninjutsu to swap in as a 3/4 attacker, maximizing combat damage against an opponent at 4 life.

annotations.description: Opus Analyst is at 1 life. Grk41F Detect has Kaito, Bane of Nightmares in hand and enough mana (4+ available from untapped lands) to cast it. During their turn, Kaito is a 3/4 hexproof creature that could attack for lethal. Opus Analyst's creatures appear mostly tapped, so Kaito would likely connect. Instead, they passed their entire turn without deploying Kaito, allowing Opus Analyst to untap and attack with 5 creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat and the turn without casting any spells, missing the opportunity to attack for lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kaito, Bane of Nightmares in the first main phase for {2}{U}{B}, then attack with Kaito as a 3/4 hexproof creature to deal lethal damage to the opponent at 1 life.
